claims.text: Hallucinations in LLMs can be distinguished into factual inaccuracies and flawed logical derivations.
Hybrid reasoning techniques improve the accountability and transparency of language model behavior.
Transparent reasoning entails risks in high-stakes decision support system applications.
A comparative framework can evaluate common explainability techniques for detecting hallucinated outputs.

evidence.description: The authors distinguish between factual inaccuracies and flawed logical derivations when investigating hallucinations as reasoning failures.
The paper argues that combining deterministic rule-based and stochastic data-driven approaches into hybrid techniques enhances transparency and accountability.
Demonstrated through a real-world use case in decision support systems in high-stakes domains.
The authors present a framework comparing common explainability techniques to detect and account for model hallucination.

methodologies.name: Dual-Paradigm Reasoning Analysis
methodologies.description: Analyzes LLM reasoning by combining deterministic rule-based and stochastic data-driven approaches.

methodologies.name: Explainability Evaluation Comparative Framework
methodologies.description: A comparative framework designed to evaluate explainability techniques on their ability to detect hallucinated model outputs.

limitations.text: Current interpretability tools including RAG, attention mechanisms, SHAP, and LIME often fail to identify the root causes of hallucination errors.

future_work.text: Utilize training data attribution, confidence calibration, and prompt-based abstention mechanisms to improve model trustworthiness.
